dinkum-3.meaning:
Every step, command block and the closing welcome survive: "So it’s
_hello_world.rs_, not _helloworld.rs_." and "You’ve officially written a Rust
program, which makes ya a Rust programmer—welcome to the club!"
dinkum-3.sense:
Terms fit: "Rust couldn’t care less" for 'it doesn't matter to Rust', "the
usual go is" for the convention, "have a squiz", "where to get a hand".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural throughout: "Righto, first thing ya do is make a directory", "good on ya!"
dinkum-3.register: Fully retold in casual Aussie but with no swearing and moderate slang; a shade under level 5, vulgarity 2.
dinkum-3.tone: Keeps the friendly, encouraging tutorial voice.
dinkum-3.flow:
Reads smoothly: "Got more than one word in yer filename? Then the
usual go is to stick an underscore between ’em."
dinkum-3.variety:
Leans on "punch in": "punch in these commands", "punch in the code from Listing 1-1", "punch in these
commands".
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the Rust book's first program, warmth intact.

unharnessed.meaning:
All steps survive; "we reckon you
make a _projects_ directory" keeps the suggestion.
unharnessed.sense:
Terms fit: "Rust couldn't give a toss where
your code lives", "the
done thing is to stick an underscore", "have a squiz back at".
unharnessed.authenticity: Mostly natural, but "chuck in this" for typing commands is odd, and "good on ya, you bloody legend!" is a stock line.
unharnessed.register: Casual Aussie with mild swearing ("you bloody legend"); moderate density, a shade under level 5.
unharnessed.flow:
Mostly smooth; "we reckon you
make a _projects_ directory" is a clumsy suggestion (needs 'should').
unharnessed.variety: Repeats "chuck in this" twice and "punch in" twice.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All steps and the welcome survive.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "bung this in", "duck back to yer terminal window", "have a squiz back at", "ways to get a hand".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural throughout: "Rust couldn't care less where yer code lives", "good on ya!"
yarn-dinkum.register: Casual Aussie with moderate slang and no swearing; a shade under level 5, vulgarity 2.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Mostly smooth; "we reckon ya make a _projects_ directory" is clumsy as a suggestion.

engine.meaning: Nothing is lost; it is the original with a few spelling changes.
engine.sense: The few swaps ("yer", "ya") carry no sense problems.
engine.authenticity:
The dialect is spliced in mechanically, with mixed forms: "enter the followin'
commands to compile'n run the file" next to "go back to your terminal window".
engine.register:
Effectively untranslated: "Regardless of your operatin' system, the string `Hello, world!` should print to
the terminal."
engine.tone: Keeps the original's tone, since it keeps the original.
engine.flow: Clunky splices: "a directory for the “Hello, world!” project" joined as "directory'n a directory", "ya just created'n enter the code".
engine.variety: The same two or three edits throughout: dropped g, "'n", "yer".

yarn-troppo.meaning: All steps survive; additions hang off the original: "Three lines. That's the lot.", "which just looks like someone sat on the keyboard", "cos Windows always has to be different", "first round's on you".
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "keep the whole box and dice in there", "don't spit the dummy" for not panicking, "Linux, macOS, and PowerShell on Windows mob".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Mostly natural ("don't spit the dummy", "the whole box and dice"), with a stock opener: "Strewth, where do I start?"
yarn-troppo.register: A full level-5 yarn, with mild swearing ("doesn't give a toss").
yarn-troppo.tone: Keeps the welcoming warmth, but the jabs ("cos Windows always has to be different") add snark the tutorial doesn't have.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads naturally: "Rust files always end in the _.rs_ extension, no exceptions."
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied openers and slang: "Righto", "So fire up a terminal", "crack open", "duck back", "have a squiz".
yarn-troppo.essence: The Rust book's first program, recognisably, but the jokes give it a cheekier character than the original's plain encouragement.

summaries.dinkum-3: A natural, faithful tutorial in Aussie voice; leans on 'punch in' and stops short of the vulgarity allowed.
summaries.unharnessed: Natural and complete with a touch of swearing; some repetition and a stock closing line.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Natural, faithful and varied; light on vulgarity for the brief.
summaries.engine: The original with mechanical dialect spellings; not a retelling.
summaries.yarn-troppo: The fullest, most varied yarn, with a stock opener and a few cheeky additions.
